facts.advisory_summary:
bytes has integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve — # Details

In the unique reclaim path of `BytesMut::reserve`, the condition
```rs
if v_capacity >= new_cap + offset
```
uses an unchecked addition. When `new_cap + offset` overflows `usize` in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing `self.cap` to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as `spare_capacity_mut()` then trust this corrupted `cap` value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB.

This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas de

expect.note: bytes 1.6.0 is in the server path (axum/hyper/h2/sqlx), but the bug (bytes_mut.rs:657-670 unique-reclaim path) needs new_cap+offset to overflow usize, i.e. reserve(additional) close to usize::MAX on 64-bit. new_cap is already checked_add'ed (bytes_mut.rs:657); hyper/h2/tokio-util/sqlx reserve amounts bounded by buffer/frame sizes (h2 frames 24-bit), so network data cannot drive reserve to ~2^64. Not attacker-triggerable.

The impact was that correctly provided CRLs would not be consulted to check revocation. With `UnknownStatusPolicy::Deny` (the default) this would lead to incorrect but safe `Error::UnknownRevocationStatus`. With `UnknownStatusPolicy::Allow` this would

expect.note: CRL distribution-point matching needs CRLs configured on a verifier; reqwest 0.12 (postmark), sqlx-core (tls_rustls.rs:131-160 builds WebPkiServerVerifier without with_crls) and axum-server (no client auth) configure none.

facts.advisory_summary:
Name constraints for URI names were incorrectly accepted — Name constraints for URI names were ignored and therefore accepted.

Note this library does not provide an API for asserting URI names, and URI name constraints are otherwise not implemented.  URI name constraints are now rejected unconditionally.

Since name constraints are restrictions on otherwise properly-issued certificates, this bug is reachable only after signature verification and requires misissuance to exploit.

This vulnerability is identified as [GHSA-965h-392x-2mh5](https://github.com/rustls/webpki/security/advisories/GHSA

expect.note: URI name constraints in webpki 0.102.6 only matter on outbound server-cert verification. rustls 0.23/rustls-webpki 0.102 client-side cert verification in the server happens only (a) via postmark->reqwest 0.12 (rustls-tls => webpki-roots) in send_verification, gated by optional mail.enabled + postmark token (user.rs:188-224; settings default mail.enable=false, settings.rs:107), or (b) sqlx-core Postgres TLS only with sslmode verify-ca/verify-full (default prefer uses DummyTlsVerifier: sqlx-core net/tls/tls_rustls.rs:116-126, sqlx-postgres connection/tls.rs:49-52). axum-server TLS (optional tls.enable) is a server without client-cert auth, so no chain verification of peer certs. Default config verifies no peer certs.

facts.advisory_summary:
rustls-webpki: Denial of service via panic on malformed CRL BIT STRING — ### Summary

`bit_string_flags()` in `src/der.rs` panics with an index-out-of-bounds when given a BIT STRING whose content is exactly `[0x00]` (one byte: zero padding bits, zero data bytes). This is reachable through the public API `BorrowedCertRevocationList::from_der()` via the `issuingDistributionPoint` CRL extension.

**Precondition**: CRL checking is opt-in in rustls-webpki. This vulnerability affects only applications that explicitly pass `RevocationOptions` to `verify_for_usage()` and load CRL bytes from a source t

expect.note: CRL BIT STRING parsing only when CRLs are supplied to the verifier; no crate in the server path calls with_crls/RevocationOptions (sqlx-core tls_rustls.rs:131-160, reqwest 0.12 default config); axum-server TLS has no client-cert verifier.

facts.advisory_summary:
Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates — Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign
intermediate public keys when the configured trust anchors allow such paths.
The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known.

Versions 0.103.16 and 0.104.0-alpha.8 reject paths containing these public keys.

expect.note: emSign distrust bypass needs outbound chain verification with emSign in the trust anchors (webpki-roots 0.26.3 via reqwest 0.12 rustls-tls / sqlx-core). rustls 0.23/rustls-webpki 0.102 client-side cert verification in the server happens only (a) via postmark->reqwest 0.12 (rustls-tls => webpki-roots) in send_verification, gated by optional mail.enabled + postmark token (user.rs:188-224; settings default mail.enable=false, settings.rs:107), or (b) sqlx-core Postgres TLS only with sslmode verify-ca/verify-full (default prefer uses DummyTlsVerifier: sqlx-core net/tls/tls_rustls.rs:116-126, sqlx-postgres connection/tls.rs:49-52). axum-server TLS (optional tls.enable) is a server without client-cert auth, so no chain verification of peer certs.

When user-provided input is provided to any type that parses with the RFC 2822 format, a denial of service attack via stack exhaustion is possible. The attack relies on formally deprecated and rarely-used features that are part of the RFC 2822 format used in a malicious manner. Ordinary, non-malicious input will never encounter this scenario.

### Patches

facts.advisory_summary:
Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync` — The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.

expect.note: No tokio::sync::broadcast use in atuin or any server-path dependency (grep of all locked crate sources: only hyper-util server/graceful.rs:306 with unit type and feature server-graceful off, and tokio-stream's generic wrapper, unused). No !Sync Clone values sent over broadcast.

expect.note: No tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd constructor call in atuin or any locked dependency source (grep across all crates in Cargo.lock outside tokio itself); server I/O uses TcpListener/TcpStream (PollEvented).

facts.advisory_summary:
Tonic has remotely exploitable denial of service vulnerability — ### Impact

When using `tonic::transport::Server` there is a remote DoS attack that can cause the server to exit cleanly on accepting a tcp/tls stream. This can be triggered via causing the accept call to error out with errors there were not covered correctly causing the accept loop to exit. 

More information can be found [here](https://github.com/hyperium/tonic/issues/1897)

### Patches

Upgrading to tonic `0.12.3` and above contains the fix. 

### Workarounds

A custom accept loop is a possible workaround.

expect.note: tonic transport::Server is used only by atuin-daemon (client-side daemon over a local socket, daemon feature); `atuin server start` (crates/atuin/src/command/server.rs) launches axum via atuin_server::launch and never starts the tonic server.

facts.advisory_summary:
Tracing logging user input may result in poisoning logs with ANSI escape sequences — ### Impact

Previous versions of tracing-subscriber were vulnerable to ANSI escape sequence injection attacks. Untrusted user input containing ANSI escape sequences could be injected into terminal output when logged, potentially allowing attackers to:

- Manipulate terminal title bars
- Clear screens or modify terminal display
- Potentially mislead users through terminal manipulation

In isolation, impact is minimal, however security issues have been found in terminal emulators that enabled an attacker to use

expect.note: Server installs tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer() with EnvFilter (crates/atuin/src/command/server.rs:33-36), ansi feature on (workspace tracing-subscriber features). Attacker-controlled strings are logged unescaped: GET /user/:username (unauthenticated) logs debug!("user not found: {}", username) inside an instrument span with the username field (handlers/user.rs:63-74); login logs login.username on DB errors (user.rs:314-327). Depends on RUST_LOG: Dockerfile default RUST_LOG=atuin::api=info would filter these, but the shipped docker-compose.yml sets RUST_LOG=info,atuin_server=debug, a common deployment.
